meaning: the ankerman, i.e. the servant of the anker or hermit
author_comment: now generally styled an anchorite; but ancre was the earlier form. Cf. Matthewman, Monkman, Priestman, Vikerman, Armetman (v. Armet), &c., all Yorkshire surnames. 'An anchor's cheer in prison be my scope': Hamlet, iii. 2. My one London Directory instance deserves to be set in full: 'Frederic Ankerman, boot-maker, 77, Provost St., Hoxton.' Probably u is a misreading for n in the following entries [Aukereswoman]. Cotgrave has ankrosse, a female hermit.
source: Poll Tax, West Riding of Yorkshire, 1379, p. 17
record_text: William Anckerman, 1379: P. T. Yorks. p. 17.

headword: Annis, Annison, Anningson, Anness, Aningson, Annin, Anning
meaning: (1) the son of Ann, from the dim. Annie; (2) the son of Agnes, popularly Annis, Annes, or Annas
author_comment: 'Pay me, quod he, or by the swete Seinte Anne': Chaucer, C. T. 7193. The variant Anningson is curious, and seems founded upon some early dim. Annin, with an excrescent g, as in Jennings; cf. Pattison and Pattinson. In general (2) must be looked upon as the parent of all these names. Annis was the popular form of Agnes from the 14th century downwards. 'Annys: propyr name (Anneys, H., Annyce, P.)—Agnes': Prompt. Parv. [Of Anish Luke, Annis Thring, Annise Teswell and Annis Brittanie:] All these cases are feminine, and represent Agnes.
modern_distribution: London, 2, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0; MDB. (Norfolk), 0, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0; (Lincoln), 1, 1, 2, 0, 1, 0, 0; (Burnley, co. Lanc.) Anningson, 1; Philadelphia, 3, 0, 0, 1, 0, 2, 1
notes: Author notes this is a feminine use of the name, representing Agnes
source: Register of St. Columb Major, p. 39
record_text: Anish Luke: Reg. St. Colomb Major, p. 39.

Annin, with an excrescent g, as in Jennings; cf. Pattison and Pattinson. In general (2) must be looked upon as the parent of all these names. Annis was the popular form of Agnes from the 14th century downwards. 'Annys: propyr name (Anneys, H., Annyce, P.)—Agnes': Prompt. Parv. [Of Anish Luke, Annis Thring, Annise Teswell and Annis Brittanie:] All these cases are feminine, and represent Agnes.
modern_distribution: London, 2, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0; MDB. (Norfolk), 0, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0; (Lincoln), 1, 1, 2, 0, 1, 0, 0; (Burnley, co. Lanc.) Anningson, 1; Philadelphia, 3, 0, 0, 1, 0, 2, 1
notes: Husband of Maria; first name in Latin genitive form as printed
source: History of Norfolk (Blomefield and Parkin), vol. iv, p. 501
record_text: Maria, uxor Johannis Annyson, 1700: ibid. p. 501.
